requirement: Validation MUST report a requirement or example with a missing closing fence or an empty body. Full names of `{req}` and `{example}` definitions MUST be unique across requirements, examples, and named definitions. Habeas MUST report every duplicate full name, including collisions involving named definitions, and identify both the duplicate declaration and the first declaration.
rationale:
I found no gaps. All the obligations are carried out in `src/evidence.rs#fn[collect_definitions]`, which `src/evidence.rs#fn[load_definitions]` (the `{impl}` item) calls. `validate_repository` is exercised by the tests, which assert on these errors, so that path uses the same code. I did not read `validate_repository` to confirm it calls `collect_definitions`.

- **Missing closing fence:** when `!block.closed`, `collect_definitions` pushes `"{source}: {kind} {name} is missing a closing colon fence"`. It covers both requirements and examples, because it checks every block.
  - `reports_a_missing_closing_colon_fence` asserts the requirement case.
  - `example_errors_include_duplicates_invalid_bodies_and_missing_tests` asserts the example case.
  - `tests/authoring_batch.rs#fn[discovery_errors_fail_before_configuration_or_inference]` asserts it through the CLI.
- **Empty body:** when the trimmed text is empty, it pushes `"{source}: {kind} {name} has no text"`.
  - `collects_missing_orphan_format_false_and_changed_line_errors` asserts the requirement case.
  - `example_errors_include_duplicates_invalid_bodies_and_missing_tests` asserts the example case.
- **Unique full names across requirements, examples and named definitions:** every block with a valid name goes through `definitions.entry(name)`, so one map covers all three kinds.
- **Report every duplicate, naming the duplicate declaration and the first:** each `Entry::Occupied` pushes `"{source}: duplicate {kind} {name}; first declared at {previous source}"`. The first declaration stays in the map, so every later collision is reported against it. The tests assert this for these pairs:
  - requirement/requirement (`rules.repeated`)
  - requirement/example (`rules.repeated`)
  - example/example (`rules.case`)
  - requirement/definition (`duplicates_involving_named_definitions_name_the_first_declaration`)
  - definition/example (`duplicates_involving_named_definitions_name_the_first_declaration`)

Other errors from the same code are specified by requirements the same code marks `{impl}`, such as `requirements.ci.identifiers` and `requirements.definitions.declaration`. They are not unspecified behavior.
